strategy.summary: Reproduce the periodic-boundary eigenvector defect in scipy.sparse.linalg.LaplacianNd (_ev1d) by building the buggy revision 04b8f858c947 from source and running the PR's modified test_eigenvectors. The buggy _ev1d returns duplicate periodic eigenvectors, so the new orthogonality and full-decomposition asserts fail; the fixed revision should pass. No version pins are documented, so versions are chosen and flagged as such.

build_commands: git clone https://github.com/scipy/scipy.git && cd scipy && git checkout 04b8f858c947 && git submodule update --init
python -m pip install -r requirements/build.txt numpy pytest
pinned_because: Python 3.11 and numpy>=2.0 are era-inferred choices; no documented constraint exists in the evidence, so they are a judgement call, not a requirement
scipy is built from the buggy commit because the defect is in the scipy source tree and only that build can exhibit it

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/sparse/linalg/tests/test_special_sparse_arrays.py::TestLaplacianNd::test_eigenvectors with bc='periodic' and grid_shape in [(6,), (2,3), (2,3,4)], plus the added orthogonality assert_allclose(eigenvectors @ eigenvectors.T, np.eye(n), atol=atol) and full decomposition assert_allclose(L, lap.toarray(), atol=atol) from the PR diff
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 04b8f858c947 the test fails with an AssertionError from assert_allclose in the orthogonality or full-decomposition check, because periodic _ev1d produces duplicate columns so V V^T is not the identity and V diag(w) V^T does not equal lap.toarray(). On the fixed revision (the PR head with the sin/cos periodic formula) the same test passes for all parametrised grid shapes and bc values.
strategy.numerical_probe: from scipy.sparse.linalg import LaplacianNd; import numpy as np; lap=LaplacianNd(grid_shape=(6,), boundary_conditions='periodic'); V=lap.eigenvectors(); w=lap.eigenvalues(); print(np.allclose(V@np.diag(w)@V.T, lap.toarray()), np.allclose(V@V.T, np.eye(6)))

input_output_examples.buggy_output: does not equal lap.toarray(); np.allclose returns False and the assertion raises AssertionError
input_output_examples.expected_output: equals lap.toarray() within atol; eigenvectors are orthonormal so V @ V.T equals np.eye(6)

risks: The bug is a pure-Python formula error, so it should not depend on platform or BLAS, but the build still needs a compiled scipy; a wheel from a different revision will not transition.

The test diff adds asserts that reference variables eigenvectors, eigenvalues, n and lap; if these are not in scope in the test_eigenvectors method on the buggy revision, the test may fail with NameError on both revisions and not transition. Check the test body before trusting the transition.

The atol value is not stated in the evidence, so the tolerance used in the test is whatever the test file defines; if atol is loose, the buggy duplicate columns could still pass or fail unpredictably. Read atol from the test file rather than assuming it.

The evidence describes n=6 with rounded printed values only; the exact correct eigenvector values are not given, so the reproduction relies on the test's identity and reconstruction checks rather than hard-coded numbers.

No sanitiser, specific architecture, or threading mode is indicated, so none is planned; if the bug were only visible under a specific architecture the transition would not occur on x86_64 Linux, and the evidence gives no sign of that.

Both numpy and scipy version constraints are unbounded in the evidence; the chosen numpy>=2.0 and Python 3.11 may differ from the era the PR was observed in, which could change numerical output only marginally and is unlikely to affect the logical transition.

oracle.reference_source: Wikipedia periodic boundary conditions reference for second-derivative eigenvectors, as cited in the PR; the test checks reconstruction of lap.toarray() and orthogonality
oracle.why: The atol value used in test_eigenvectors is not stated in the evidence, so the tolerance is unknown here and must be read from the test file

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The orthogonality check eigenvectors @ eigenvectors.T vs np.eye(n) and the full-decomposition check V diag(w) V^T vs lap.toarray() both raise AssertionError on the buggy revision, because periodic _ev1d returns duplicate eigenvector columns (e.g. repeated rows 0.289/-0.577 for n=6), which makes V non-orthogonal and the reconstruction wrong.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the periodic eigenvectors use sin(pi(k+0.5)/n*(j+1)) for even j+1 and cos(pi(k+0.5)/n*j) otherwise, giving an orthonormal basis, so both assert_allclose checks pass within atol for all parametrised shapes and bc values.
